PullRequest.Title: chat: move plugin marketplace management to Customizations
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary
- Move plugin marketplace management from a quick pick to a Marketplaces subpage under Plugins, with all entry points opening the same page.
- Preserve marketplace browsing, refresh, removal, and the existing provider/configuration behavior.
- Improve keyboard and screen-reader guidance, announce successful removal, and use the Customizations search placeholder wording.
- Clear inventory on harness/session changes and reject stale row or open-menu actions; preserve load errors and Retry while search changes.
- Extend the component fixture to show default, user-added, organization-managed, and unavailable marketplaces, with the CI-reported Light screenshot hash.

## Testing
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/pluginMarketplacesWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed (136 tests).
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/pluginMarketplacesWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/pluginMarketplacesWidget.test.ts` — passed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: AgentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.refresh explicitly calls fireMarketplacesChanged(), which synchronously fires both subscribed events. All three widget refresh paths reach listPluginMarketplaces and the SDK RPC without a shared pending request. Call count is statically established; inventory size and RPC duration are not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Agent Host inventory IPC calls, Copilot SDK marketplace-list RPC calls, and mapped inventory objects.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For K completed marketplace refresh actions, the widget performs 3K inventory reads instead of K, each returning and mapping M marketplaces. The pending set limits mutations per marketplace ID, not inventory reads shared across IDs. Existing workbench-service inventory reads are additional but unchanged and are not attributed to this finding.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess IPC/RPC traffic and full-inventory allocation, with redundant work on the post-action refresh path.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The quick-pick management loop awaited provider.refresh and then listed the inventory once on the next loop iteration. Existing workbench marketplace-service event subscriptions could also list, but those subscriptions remain unchanged.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A single provider marketplace refresh now starts three inventory reads in the widget instead of one: two from the provider's paired change events and one from runEntry's finally block. Incrementing generation suppresses older results but does not coalesce or cancel their IPC/RPC work.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added provider.onDidChange and provider.onDidChangeMarketplaces subscriptions at pluginMarketplacesWidget.ts:253-254 both immediately invoke refresh(), which calls provider.list at line 318. The added runEntry finally block at line 467 invokes it a third time. Previously the deleted manageProviderMarketplaces loop issued one provider.list when returning from Refresh Marketplace.
Findings.Title: Coalesce the three inventory reads triggered by one marketplace refresh
Findings.Impact: Using Refresh Marketplace in the visible Copilot marketplace page performs two avoidable inventory IPC/RPC round trips and full-inventory transformations per action. Repeated refreshes or refreshing several different marketplaces increase backend traffic and allocation pressure; the page's final refresh completion awaits the third read rather than using the already-started authoritative read.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.ts:107-110 fires both events; its refresh method at 224-230 calls that helper after the mutation. Its list method at 149-153 forwards to agentHostService.listPluginMarketplaces. LocalAgentHostService.ts:675-676 and AgentHostManagementService.ts:237-241 forward each call independently, and CopilotAgent.ts:3800-3804 / CopilotAgentSession.ts:1351-1352 issue plugins.marketplaces.list RPCs. PluginMarketplacesWidget.refresh has no in-flight guard and only discards stale results after listing and mapping the entire inventory (318-342).
Findings.Recommendation: Coalesce the paired provider events and the post-action refresh into one session/provider-scoped scheduled or in-flight inventory read. Let runEntry await that shared post-mutation refresh; retain generation checks and ensure a later mutation marks the inventory dirty for a subsequent read.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Marketplaces through the command, Discover, or Plugins; close or reopen the Customizations editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared command awaits opening the editor. showPluginMarketplaces then reveals the new widget and starts its inventory refresh asynchronously. Marketplace rows require that refresh to finish; the editor shell does not await it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List the selected session's provider-owned marketplaces through the management IPC proxy and Copilot SDK marketplace-list RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One widget inventory read per transition to visible, returning all M marketplaces. Existing workbench source inventory reads are separate and unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The management quick pick awaited one provider.list before displaying its inventory. This PR moves that existing inventory operation into the subpage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to populate marketplace rows, not to display the editor shell.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Briefly activate the installed-plugin view and read the session customization item source before switching to Marketplaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra consumer call per activation; ProviderItemSource and PureItemProviderItemSource reuse their cachedPromise, including in-flight requests, across consumers. No per-plugin transport fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The standalone management quick pick did not activate the installed-plugin widget. Ordinary section navigation already used this cached item source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous installed-item refresh is not awaited by marketplace navigation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M configured/provider marketplaces and the existing session customization inventory. The new tree renders only viewport rows; constructors create one widget per editor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventory loading is asynchronous without a widget-level limiter. Generation checks reject obsolete results. The transient installed-item refresh shares the item source's in-flight promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The marketplace widget does not cache or coalesce provider.list across visibility transitions. Session customization item sources share cached promises and invalidate on provider changes. Hidden marketplace refresh calls return before listing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in visibility gating, asynchronous row loading, and the item-source promise cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold editor construction and inventory RPC durations are unmeasured. The additional hidden tree/control construction is bounded; no independently significant constructor fan-out was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Moving management into an editor intentionally adds editor UI construction. No separate high-confidence regression established for initial navigation; repeated refresh coalescing is reported in the mutation scenario.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh or remove a provider-owned marketplace while the Marketplaces subpage remains visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected mutation must finish before success is announced. runEntry then awaits an inventory refresh. Paired provider events start two other inventory refreshes immediately after the mutation; their obsolete results are discarded rather than their work being cancelled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the selected marketplace or remove it through Agent Host management IPC and the SDK RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh RPC per action. Removal uses one RPC normally or a second forced-removal RPC after explicit confirmation. Each targets one marketplace name, not every inventory entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The quick-pick actions invoked the same provider refresh/remove operations and the same optional forced removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mutation completion is required for the action to finish. Existing removal may reload runtime customizations before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeatedly list and transform the complete marketplace inventory after one mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The widget starts three reads from the demonstrated paths: onDidChangeMarketplaces, onDidChange, and runEntry finally. Additional general customization notifications may also refresh it. For K refresh actions, this proves at least 3K widget reads of M entries versus K quick-pick loop reads. The existing workbench source service's paired-event reads are unchanged and excluded from the finding's added-work count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After provider.refresh, the old management loop listed once on its next iteration. Inline removal could remove a quick-pick item without relisting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The final widget read is awaited on the post-action path; the two already-started reads consume IPC/RPC and allocations without providing the authoritative final render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K marketplace mutations and M marketplaces per returned inventory, not one read per marketplace row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Different marketplace IDs can be operated on independently. The paired event callbacks launch concurrent inventory reads, and the final read overlaps them. The traced management and Copilot list implementations forward each read independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No widget pending-list promise or list-result cache. The pending set coalesces mutations only for the same marketplace ID; generations suppress stale results after the full read and mapping. Successful and failed mutation paths both reach the finally refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: provider.fireMarketplacesChanged explicitly emits both subscribed events, provider.list forwards to IPC/RPC, and runEntry always refreshes afterward.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: M and SDK RPC duration vary and are unmeasured. The deterministic duplicate-call mechanism is independent of those magnitudes; severity is low.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one introduced missing-coalescing regression for redundant inventory IPC/RPC and allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add a marketplace directly or from the new page, including validation, cancellation, and retry.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider inventory is awaited before the source prompt for duplicate validation. A successful add must finish before the prompt closes and the shared management command opens/reveals the page. Cancelled prompts do not reopen management.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read configured sources, add one provider marketplace, and verify its presence through the backend's inventory read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-prompt list; one add per accepted attempt; the existing Copilot add implementation performs one verification list. Successful adds emit both provider change events, causing two widget lists if the page is visible, plus a list when the management command hides/reveals that page. Existing workbench source event reads remain separate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct provider addition already awaited inventory, invoked the same add/verification path, and returned to management with a fresh list. The new visible-page subscriptions add duplicate post-add reads, the same coalescing root cause as the reported finding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pre-prompt inventory delays showing the prompt. Mutation and backend verification delay success. Event-driven widget lists occur after mutation and are not awaited by the source prompt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist an added configuration-backed source to chat.plugins.marketplaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update per successful add; inline validation parses source strings without I/O.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local addition likewise persisted one updated configuration array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write is awaited before the prompt closes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M existing sources for validation and the number of explicitly accepted add attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One accepted add at a time per prompt. Post-add inventory event reads are uncoalesced; source validation itself is synchronous and local.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Duplicate validation now uses a Set of parsed canonical IDs. Provider inventory is still read before prompting; no new per-keystroke IPC. Busy state prevents overlapping add submissions; cancellation disposes prompt listeners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the action diff, prompt busy/disposal guards, and backend add verification implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and configuration write duration are unmeasured. No additional independent issue beyond the reported duplicate-list root cause.
Scenarios.Verdict: Preserves the existing mutation and pre-prompt boundary count. Duplicate page refreshes share the reported root cause; no second finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manage configuration-backed marketplaces: explicitly refresh one, open its folder, or remove it.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Refresh awaits the selected marketplace fetch. Open Folder awaits file existence only after that action is chosen. Removal awaits one configuration update; local inventory rerender uses configuration reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Force-refresh the selected GitHub marketplace definition using resolveRef and definition-file requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A singleton marketplace-ID set restricts the fetch to one canonical marketplace. Requests cover the fixed supported definition paths; private/unreadable repositories may use clone fallback. Returned plugins can number P.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configuration-backed management did not expose this refresh action. Existing plugin browsing already used these fetch implementations. The newly exposed operation is user-requested and scoped, not accidental fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit refresh action awaits completion; unrelated marketplace inventories are not fetched by this action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare or update one clone using shared-process local Git operations, followed by definition-file reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected repository; cold state may clone, warm forced refresh may pull/fetch. Candidate cache paths are deduplicated. Authentication fallback can retry the operation using existing logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This boundary was already used by browsing but was not available as a configuration-backed management refresh action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Clone/update and definition reads are awaited by the explicit refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check a repository folder, reveal it if present, or persist removal from user marketplace configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fileService.exists only when Open Folder is selected; one reveal command if present. One configuration update per removal. No per-row existence checks during rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old management flow checked folder existence before showing the marketplace action picker and performed the same reveal/removal operations. The existence check is now deferred to the chosen folder action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the selected action awaits the corresponding operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected canonical repository per refresh, P plugins in its definition, and M configuration references parsed to rebuild the inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The widget blocks duplicate mutations for the same marketplace ID. Different IDs can run concurrently. Git preparation uses SequencerByKey per repository operation key, not a global limiter. This is user-driven rather than an automatic all-repository burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Explicit refresh bypasses the GitHub marketplace cache and uses refreshIfOlderThanMs=0 for clone-backed repositories. Local file repositories only check existence before reading definitions. Ordinary fetches retain the existing TTL/index behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in singleton selection, cache bypass for explicit refresh, per-repository sequencing, and deferred folder I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, authentication fallback, Git duration, and definition sizes are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: New refresh work is intentional, explicit, and scoped to the selected marketplace. No independent high-confidence regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse one marketplace or Browse All from the new management page.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Navigation executes the existing OpenMarketplace command. Discover can render cached previews, while selected source queries must settle to deliver refreshed available results. Marketplace management hides and stops subsequent inventory reloads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browse each selected provider marketplace through its SDK browse RPC; enabled public-feed browsing uses existing saved-feed SDK operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One marketplace browse operation per selected provider per requested page; selecting one source reaches one provider, while Browse All reaches S applicable sources. Provider browse returns its full P-plugin inventory before filtering/slicing. Public-feed calls are grouped by the fixed configured saved feeds, not by individual result cards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old Browse and Browse All quick-pick actions executed the same OpenMarketplace command with the same source selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Source results depend on those operations; cached previews can appear before they finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch selected configuration-backed marketplace definitions, using GitHub content APIs or existing clone/file fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One canonical marketplace ID per internal plugin provider; selecting S configured sources reaches S distinct repositories. Plugin-service continuation state and GitHub TTL cache can avoid repeated underlying fetches; no new per-result requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing selected/all browsing used the same provider composition and source query operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold source loading waits for those fetches; cached previews reduce time to first content.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S enabled/selected sources and P plugins per provider inventory, with page sizes bounded by the existing marketplace service.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The shared marketplace service uses Promise.all for eligible provider queries and emits progress as sources settle. Git operations remain serialized per repository. The diff does not change these scheduling rules.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing browse-cache keys include provider ID, media type, and page size, with ten-minute previews; cached pages are revalidated. GitHub marketplace content uses its existing TTL cache. Source changes invalidate caches. No new cache keys or lifetimes introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from identical command arguments and the traced existing source/provider call chain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Source count and cold-network latency vary. Full provider-inventory browse behavior is pre-existing, not attributed to the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: Entry-point refactor only; no changed browsing cardinality, cache lifecycle, or transport mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search, keyboard navigation, accessibility reading, resize, harness/session changes, and hidden-page lifetime.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Search filters and rebuilds the local tree synchronously. Layout measures the visible container and lays out viewport rows. Harness/session changes clear entries, bind new provider listeners, and asynchronously reload only when visible.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: M marketplace entries per local filter/tree-model rebuild, viewport-sized rendered rows, input frequency, and session changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Search/render/layout run on the UI thread. ResizeObserver handles header changes. In-flight list results are rejected with generations; no separate unbounded retained cache was introduced. Pending mutations remain tracked until their finally blocks execute.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Search and accessibility use the already-loaded entries and do not query providers. Errors and Retry persist across search changes. Hidden refresh calls are no-ops. Harness autorun store replaces provider listeners; editor disposal releases the tree, hovers, observer, and row action stores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that search is local, row DOM is virtualized, hidden loading is gated, and listener/template ownership is disposable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: M is ordinarily a marketplace configuration list rather than a result/plugin catalog; very large lists are possible but no high-confidence significant rendering regression was established. Static review does not quantify layout costs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independently reportable synchronous-layout or retention regression. The new fixture/test data and screenshot reference do not add production runtime work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the complete 14-file inventory and all diff pages. Submitted one low-severity, high-confidence missing-coalescing finding for redundant provider inventory IPC/RPC after mutations. Traced navigation, provider/local mutations, browsing, cache behavior, concurrency, rendering, and disposal. Other candidates were intentional scoped feature work, cache-coalesced existing consumers, bounded UI construction, or pre-existing mechanisms. Static read-only review; no profiling measurements or qualifying regression-fix provenance signal.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
